theorems.explanation: The square of the area density is the two-by-two Gram determinant. Mathlib identifies the same determinant with the square of normDet. Expanding the Gram determinant and using symmetry of the real inner product gives equality of squares. Both quantities are nonnegative, hence they are equal. The area-density square and nonnegativity lemmas are retained as local helpers.

payload.natural_language_statement:
Let $E$ be a two-dimensional real inner product space, let $F$ be any real inner product space, and let $L:E\to F$ be linear. For every orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2)$ of $E$,

$$\sqrt{\|Le_1\|^2\|Le_2\|^2-\langle Le_1,Le_2\rangle^2}=\operatorname{normDet}(L).$$

theorems.explanation: Expand each vector of the second basis in the first basis. Distribute the bilinear map in both arguments and exchange the finite sums. Parseval collapses the sum of products of change-of-basis coefficients to an inner product of first-basis vectors. Orthonormality makes that inner product a Kronecker delta, leaving exactly the first diagonal sum. The two proof-side private helpers are preserved.

    ∑ i, B (b i) (b i) = ∑ i, B (b' i) (b' i) := by sorry
payload.natural_language_statement:
Let $V$ be a real inner product space with two orthonormal bases $(b_i)_{i\in I}$ and $(c_j)_{j\in J}$, indexed by arbitrary finite types $I,J$. Let $W$ be any real module and $B:V\times V\to W$ a bilinear map. Then

$$\sum_{i\in I}B(b_i,b_i)=\sum_{j\in J}B(c_j,c_j).$$

The bilinear map need not be symmetric, and the target module need not carry an inner product. This is the basis-independence of the diagonal contraction.
